newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Growth seen for Amsterdam Exchanges' New Market.
newsitem.headline: Growth seen for Amsterdam Exchanges' New Market.

text.p: Various companies in which Dutch venture capital firms have interests are considering a listing on the recently launched New Market of the Amsterdam Exchanges (NMAX), chairman Sam Alleman of the association of Dutch venture capital firms (NVP) said on Thursday.
"About 10 to 20 of these companies have plans for a flotation," he told reporters.
NVP secretary Frank Claassen added that a survey among NVP members showed that about half of these firms were expected to take this step within the next two years.
Amsterdam's New Market was launched earlier this year and is intended for young and fast growing companies with international ambitions.
The market now lists three companies, software firms CSS and PolyDoc and gearbox maker Antonov.
Alleman said NMAX was "viable" but press reports of hundreds of companies lining up for a listing were unrealistic.
It sometimes looked as if every company was eying a bourse listing, but the vast majority of them would never take the step, he added.
Alleman said the venture capital firms did not see NMAX and other new securities exchanges in Europe as a threat because of rising competition in the markets for risk bearing capital.
These exchanges' target groups were bordering fairly close to those of venture capitalists, so that the new markets were seen rather as a welcome addition.
These markets also offer a good channel to sell interests or parts of them, thus expanding the exit possibilities of capital venture firms.
"It is a trend which we greet with pleasure," Alleman said.
